# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.sh from the help texts in src/cli; run `just docs` instead of editing. -->

The `--help` of every command. Guides: [Applications](Applications.md), [Servers and shared apps](Servers-and-Shared-Apps.md), [Backup and restore](Backup-and-Restore.md).

Exit codes: `0` OK · `1` unexpected error · `2` invalid local config or usage · `3` server not ready or a server-side check failed · `4` deployed, but not healthy · `130` interrupted with Ctrl-C.

## `compost`

```text
Manage docker-based server deployments

Usage: compost [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init        Create the local compost home with a new (or the given) manager key
  server      Define, inspect and deploy servers
  connect     Use <NAME> as the default server for following commands
  disconnect  Forget the default server
  app         Deploy and inspect user applications
  connector   Inspect links between applications and shared apps
  backup      Inspect backups
  secret      Store application secrets on the server for `app deploy`
  config      Set and show preferences, e.g. `deploy.apply`
  agent       Documentation for AI agents: llms.txt, llms-full.txt and an Agent Skill
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

## `compost init`

```text
Create the local compost home with a new (or the given) manager key

Usage: compost init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --key <KEY>        Use this manager key (a UUID) instead of a new one, e.g. to manage the servers of another compost installation from this machine
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --force            Replace the manager key of an initialized home
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server`

```text
Define, inspect and deploy servers

Usage: compost server [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Write starter compost-server.yaml, compost-server.prod.yaml and a secrets example
  define    Add or replace a server in the local configuration
  list      List defined servers
  state     Check and display server state
  deploy    Deploy shared applications from compost-server.yaml
  backup    Back up shared applications (data, configuration and secrets)
  restore   Restore shared applications from a server backup
  logs      Show the output of a shared application's containers
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server generate`

```text
Write starter compost-server.yaml, compost-server.prod.yaml and a secrets example

Usage: compost server generate [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --list             List the shared app types that can be generated
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --with <WITH>      Shared app types to include, e.g. `caddy,postgres` (asked when not given)
      --force            Overwrite existing files
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server define`

```text
Add or replace a server in the local configuration

Usage: compost server define [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Server name used in other commands

Options:
      --address <ADDRESS>              Host name or IP address (SSH)
  -s, --server <SERVER>                Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --user <USER>                    SSH user [default: compostuser]
  -v, --verbose                        Print every command run on the server
      --port <PORT>                    SSH port
      --identity-file <IDENTITY_FILE>  SSH private key (default: ssh config, agent, ~/.ssh/id_*)
      --server-home <SERVER_HOME>      compost directory on the server (default ~/.compost-server)
      --local                          Manage this machine instead of a remote server
      --force                          Replace an existing server with the same name
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## `compost server deploy`

```text
Deploy shared applications from compost-server.yaml

Usage: compost server deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply            Also start or restart services (default: `deploy.apply`, see `compost config`)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --no-apply         Only upload files, even when `deploy.apply` is set
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --dry-run          Validate and show what would change on the server, without changing it
      --diff             With --dry-run: also show the changed lines of files without secrets
      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
      --pull             Pull images again, even when their tags did not change, and build images built on the server on newer base images (needs `--apply`)
      --recreate         Recreate every container, even unchanged ones; data in volumes is kept (needs `--apply`)
      --secret <FILE>    Overlay with secrets (e.g. .compost-server.secrets.yaml) to store on the server and deploy with, replacing the stored one; later deploys use it without the file
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost server backup`

```text
Back up shared applications (data, configuration and secrets)

Usage: compost server backup [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --shared <SHARED>
          Only this shared app (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --format <FORMAT>
          `compost` (restorable archive) or `raw` (plain files: one as is, several as tar.gz)
          
          [default: compost]
          [possible values: compost, raw]

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output file or folder (with `--target server`: a file name in the server's backup folder)

      --target <TARGET>
          Where to write (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost server restore`

```text
Restore shared applications from a server backup

Usage: compost server restore [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVE>

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVE>
          Archive written by `compost server backup` (with `--source server`: a file in the server's backup folder)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --shared <SHARED>
          Only this shared app (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --source <SOURCE>
          Where the archive is (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --yes
          Do not ask for confirmation

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost server logs`

```text
Show the output of a shared application's containers

Usage: compost server logs [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Shared app, as in compost-server.yaml, e.g. `caddy-main` (`<kind>/<name>` if two kinds use the name)

Options:
      --follow           Keep streaming new output until Ctrl-C
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --tail <TAIL>      Lines to show from the end of each container's output, or `all` [default: 100]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --since <SINCE>    Only output since this time: a duration like `10m` or a time like `2026-10-17T12:00:00`
      --timestamps       Show the time of every line
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost app`

```text
Deploy and inspect user applications

Usage: compost app [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Write a starter compost.yaml and .compost.secrets.example.yaml from the compose file
  list      List the application instances deployed on the server
  deploy    Deploy the application instance described by the given files
  state     Show the state of an application instance
  logs      Show the output of an application instance's containers
  remove    Remove an application instance
  backup    Back up an application instance (or all of them)
  restore   Restore an application instance from a compost backup
  releases  List the releases of an application instance kept for rollback
  rollback  Deploy an earlier release of an application instance again, with the images it ran
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -h, --help             Print help
```

```text
Write a starter compost.yaml and .compost.secrets.example.yaml from the compose file

  -s, --server <SERVER>              Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --name <NAME>                  Application name (default: the current directory's name)
```

## `compost app deploy`

```text
Deploy the application instance described by the given files

Usage: compost app deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --apply            Also start or restart services (default: `deploy.apply`, see `compost config`)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --no-apply         Only upload files, even when `deploy.apply` is set
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --dry-run          Validate and show what would change on the server, without changing it
      --diff             With --dry-run: also show the changed lines of files without secrets
      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
      --pull             Pull images again, even when their tags did not change, and build images built on the server on newer base images (needs `--apply`)
      --recreate         Recreate every container, even unchanged ones; data in volumes is kept (needs `--apply`)
      --prefix <PREFIX>  Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --purge <PURGE>    Also delete the data of links dropped from the config, for these kinds, e.g. `--purge database`
      --secret <FILE>    Overlay with secrets (e.g. .compost.secrets.yaml) to store on the server and deploy with, replacing the stored one; later deploys use it without the file
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost app remove`

```text
Remove an application instance

Usage: compost app remove [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]  Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --app <APP>        Application name (instead of config files)
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --prefix <PREFIX>  Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)

      --purge <PURGE>    Delete the instance's data held by these kinds, e.g. `--purge database`

      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `compost app backup`

```text
Back up an application instance (or all of them)

Usage: compost app backup [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]
          Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>
          Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)

  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --app <APP>
          Application name (instead of config files)

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --prefix <PREFIX>
          Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)

      --all
          Back up every instance on the server into one archive

      --include <INCLUDE>
          Parts to save (default: links,sources,volumes; only links with --link)

          Possible values:
          - links:   Data and configuration of links (database dumps, ingress sites)
          - sources: Uploaded sources (only the compose file when sources are not uploaded)
          - volumes: Named volumes listed under `backup.volumes`
          - images:  Docker images of the services, as `docker save` writes them

      --link <LINK>
          Only this link: `<entry>` or `<kind>:<entry>` (repeatable)

      --format <FORMAT>
          `compost` (restorable archive) or `raw` (plain files: one as is, several as tar.gz)
          
          [default: compost]
          [possible values: compost, raw]

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output file or folder (with `--target server`: a file name in the server's backup folder)

      --target <TARGET>
          Where to write (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

      --stop
          Stop every service while volumes are copied, for a consistent copy (default: those in `backup.stop`)

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost app restore`

```text
Restore an application instance from a compost backup

Usage: compost app restore [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVE>

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVE>
          Archive written by `compost app backup` (with `--source server`: a file in the server's backup folder)

Options:
      --instance <INSTANCE>
          Instance in the archive, e.g. `myapp-staging` (needed when it has several)

  -s, --server <SERVER>
          Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context)
          
          [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]

      --all
          Restore every instance in the archive

  -v, --verbose
          Print every command run on the server

      --prefix <PREFIX>
          Restore under this prefix, e.g. to make a copy

  -f, --file <FILES>
          Overlays merged over the archived config, e.g. other domains (repeatable or comma-separated)

      --include <INCLUDE>
          Parts to restore (default: all in the archive; only links with --link). Without `sources`, data is loaded into the deployed instance

          Possible values:
          - links:   Data and configuration of links (database dumps, ingress sites)
          - sources: Uploaded sources (only the compose file when sources are not uploaded)
          - volumes: Named volumes listed under `backup.volumes`
          - images:  Docker images of the services, as `docker save` writes them

      --link <LINK>
          Only this link: `<entry>` or `<kind>:<entry>` (repeatable)

      --source <SOURCE>
          Where the archive is (default: `backup.target` of compost-server.yaml, else local)

          Possible values:
          - local:  This machine; data is streamed through the connector
          - server: A folder on the server
          - s3:     An S3 bucket (not implemented yet)

      --replace
          Overwrite databases and volumes that already hold data

      --yes
          Do not ask for confirmation

      --force-unlock
          Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `compost app rollback`

```text
Deploy an earlier release of an application instance again, with the images it ran

Usage: compost app rollback [OPTIONS] [INSTANCE]

Arguments:
  [INSTANCE]  Instance as shown by `app list`, e.g. `myapp-staging`

Options:
  -f, --file <FILES>     Config files merged in order (repeatable or comma-separated)
  -s, --server <SERVER>  Target server (default: `COMPOST_SERVER`, then the current context) [env: COMPOST_SERVER=]
      --app <APP>        Application name (instead of config files)
  -v, --verbose          Print every command run on the server
      --prefix <PREFIX>  Instance prefix (overrides the one from the config files)
      --to <RELEASE>     Release to deploy, as `app releases` shows it (default: the one before the current release)
      --dry-run          Show what would change without changing anything
      --yes              Do not ask for confirmation
      --force-unlock     Remove a lock left behind by an interrupted compost command
  -h, --help             Print help
```
